title: Kitchen-Sink Cookies
summary: Thick, chewy cookies loaded with chocolate, pretzels, crisps and biscuit pieces for a salty-sweet crunch in every bite.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
dark chocolate chips or chunks (50-60% cocoa solids)
salted pretzels, broken into 1 cm pieces
plain salted crisps (potato chips), lightly crushed
digestive biscuits or graham crackers, broken into chunks

steps.title: Cream butter and sugars
steps.text: Beat the softened butter, both sugars and the golden syrup together on medium speed for 2-3 minutes, until pale and fluffy. This creaming step beats air into the dough, which helps give the baked cookies some lift rather than a dense, flat texture. Beat in the egg and vanilla for about a minute until fully combined.

steps.title: Add the dry ingredients
steps.text: Add the flour, oats, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt on low speed, mixing just until combined. Then fold in the chocolate, pretzels, crisps, digestive biscuit pieces and coffee granules on the lowest speed for only a few seconds. Mixing the mix-ins any longer than that smashes the crisps and pretzels to dust instead of leaving them in recognisable crunchy pieces.

steps.title: Chill the dough
steps.text: Scoop the dough into 55 g balls onto a lined tray, cover, and chill for at least 1 hour, up to 3 days. Cold, rested dough spreads less in the oven and stays thicker, which matters for a cookie carrying this much weight in mix-ins. The chill also gives the oats time to soften slightly.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) for at least 20 minutes, with a shelf in the middle. A fully heated oven helps these thick, heavily loaded cookies set around the edges quickly, which stops them spreading too thin under the weight of all the extras.

steps.title: Bake one tray at a time
steps.text: Bake six cookies per tray, one tray at a time, for 13-15 minutes, until the edges are golden and the centres still look pale and soft. Baking only one tray at once keeps the heat even across all six cookies, rather than splitting it between two trays. The pale, soft centre at this stage will firm up as the cookies cool, so don't wait for it to look fully set.

steps.title: Cool carefully
steps.text: Leave the cookies on the tray for 10 minutes before moving them, since they're fragile with all the mix-ins until they've had a chance to firm up. Transfer to a wire rack to finish cooling. Makes about 18 cookies.

tips: Fold in the mix-ins on the lowest speed for only a few seconds — overmixing is a common mistake that pulverises the pretzels and crisps instead of leaving them crunchy.
Chill the scooped dough for at least an hour; skipping this gives thinner, more spread-out cookies that lose the contrast between chewy dough and crunchy extras.
Use plain salted crisps, not flavoured ones, so the seasoning doesn't clash with the chocolate.
Bake one tray at a time for the most even results, especially since these cookies are thicker than a standard batch.
Leave the cookies to cool on the tray for the full 10 minutes — moving them too soon can break them apart around the mix-ins.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 4 days. Scooped raw dough balls freeze well for up to 3 months — bake from frozen, adding 2-3 minutes to the time.
